question: Participant-level size distribution for the Chariot/K2D 2026 DAF Fundraising Report: look in the report PDF, the webinar recording or slides, and Chariot's earlier editions for the 54 participants' size bands, sector mix, the number of participant-years (balanced or unbalanced 2021-25 panel) and the pooled-vs-median DAF share by size; then re-weight the filing domain to that distribution instead of matching on the $96.7m mean
conclusion_affected: Whether Chariot's 12.6% is above the filing estimate for comparable organisations (size-matched central pooled ~10% on 1h-1d-1e)
rationale: The mean of $26.1bn / 54 / 5 = $96.7m can come from very different distributions. A pooled share is dominated by the largest participants, and the filing domain's pooled share falls with size (b3avg 25-100m vs >=100m in the CSV), so the matching variable matters more than the band edges

question: Named-participant check: for organisations the Chariot webinar names as study participants (ACLU; No Kid Hungry / Share Our Strength) read FY2023-24 Form 990 Part VIII and the all-panel Schedule I numerator for every related EIN (ACLU Inc, ACLU Foundation, Share Our Strength), and compare filing-based DAF share with each organisation's published DAF figures
conclusion_affected: Whether CRM-coded DAF revenue and Schedule I DAF grants agree at the same organisation (numerator definition gap vs selection)
rationale: The size-matched gap could be selection (opt-in DAFpay clients) or numerator definition. A named-organisation reconciliation separates the two. ACLU Foundation is in the size-matched domain with a high filing share (central 35% of 1h-1d-1e)

question: Intermediary screen for the recipient frame: classify the certainty-stratum recipients with filing shares above 50% on 1h-1d-1e (e.g. The 85 Fund, Hopewell Fund, Our American Future Foundation, San Antonio Valley Ranch LLC, Bright Funds Foundation) as operating charity, fiscal sponsor, re-granting fund or DAF-like vehicle from their Schedule I and mission statement, and re-run size-banded shares excluding re-granters
conclusion_affected: Size-matched and >=$100m pooled shares; Chariot comparison
rationale: In the $50m-$200m domain the largest leave-one-out influence is a re-granting fund (The 85 Fund). The name/NTEE-T screen used by the repo does not catch Hopewell or 50CAN-type entities, and Chariot's participants are fundraising charities

question: Add a revenue-weighted (pooled) and an organisation-weighted (median) version of every size band to the central scenario, using own Part VIII 1h-1d-1e as the banding variable instead of BMF REVENUE_AMT, for $1m-$5m, $5m-$25m and $25m-$100m too; replace the BMF-band table in b40n1202-b43n26 s2.2 where the change exceeds the interval
conclusion_affected: Size gradient of the DAF share (b40n1202-b43n26 s2.2) and its use against Chariot's <$10m participants (NPB024)
rationale: BMF revenue band and own-contribution band disagree at the top (the $50m-$200m BMF band has about twice the respondents of the contribution band), so the existing band table mixes government-funded and contribution-funded organisations

question: Supplementary sample in the $50m-$200m contribution band: draw extra non-certainty recipients from the committed frame with BMF revenue >=$25m (strata d and e) and read their Part VIII, to cut the bootstrap interval on the size-matched pooled share below +-2 points
rationale: About half of the domain's respondents are certainty units; the rest come from two BMF-band strata of 40, so the domain interval is several points wide
